title: Parseval's Identity
body:
**Energy in the time domain equals energy in the frequency domain.** For a [[Fourier Series]],

$$
\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}|f(x)|^2\,dx = \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}|c_n|^2
$$

and in trigonometric form $\frac{1}{\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} f^2\,dx = \frac{a_0^2}{2} + \sum(a_n^2 + b_n^2)$.
The transform moves the information around but does not create or destroy any of it.

This is the Pythagorean theorem on an [[Orthonormal Basis]]: the squared length of a vector is the
sum of the squares of its coordinates, and the [[Fourier Coefficients]] are the coordinates. See
[[Inner Product]] and [[Vector Norm]] in [[LINEAR ALGEBRA FOR DATA SCIENCE]] for the
finite-dimensional statement, which is the same theorem with a finite sum.

Two consequences worth keeping. It says $\sum|c_n|^2$ converges, so the coefficients must go to
zero. And it is how you decide **which coefficients to throw away**: dropping the ones with the
smallest $|c_n|^2$ loses the least energy, which is the entire principle behind lossy compression
and the same argument [[Low-Rank Approximation]] makes with singular values.
